title: Room-temperature Magnetoelastic Coupling in UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$
authors: Mingyu Xu, Tomasz Klimczuk, M. Brian Maple, Weiwei Xie
abstract: The interplay between electronic and structural degrees of freedom underpins many emergent phenomena in quantum materials, yet magnetoelastic coupling in metallic systems is typically weak and confined to low temperatures or microscopic length scales. Here, we report giant magnetoelastic coupling slightly above room temperature in the uranium-based intermetallic compound UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$. Using temperature-dependent single-crystal X-ray diffraction together with anisotropic magnetic susceptibility measurements, we directly resolve subtle but reproducible structural distortions coupled to magnetic alignment. Despite the absence of crystallographic symmetry breaking, pronounced anomalies emerge in lattice parameters and selected chemical bond distances near the magnetic transition region, revealing an unusual sensitivity of the crystal structure to magnetic orientation. The coupling enables direct probing of how atomic distances and local chemical bonding govern the electronic and magnetic states in a bulk intermetallic material. Our results establish UIr$_4$Al$_{15}$ as a rare platform in which magnetism and lattice distortions are strongly intertwined near room temperature, opening new opportunities for magnetically responsive quantum materials and functional magnetic sensing applications.
summary: This experimental work reports on giant magnetoelastic coupling in the uranium compound UIr4Al15, observed slightly above room temperature. By combining single-crystal X-ray diffraction with magnetic measurements, the authors show that the magnetic anomaly correlates precisely with abrupt, anisotropic changes in local atomic bond distances. This establishes the material as a key platform for studying bond-driven magnetoelastic effects in correlated quantum materials.
main_problem: Investigating the origin of a magnetic anomaly near room temperature in the metallic intermetallic compound UIr4Al15, specifically determining if it is driven by magnetoelastic coupling.
main_result: The magnetic anomaly strongly correlates with abrupt, anisotropic structural changes observed via X-ray diffraction, suggesting a bond-driven magnetoelastic coupling mechanism.
method: The study combines temperature-dependent single-crystal X-ray diffraction with anisotropic magnetic susceptibility and specific heat measurements.
model_or_system: The physical system is the uranium-based intermetallic compound UIr4Al15, which is characterized by its crystal structure (P42/nmc) and the interplay between its electronic, magnetic, and structural degrees of freedom.
key_observables: Lattice parameters, specific chemical bond distances (e.g., U-Ir bonds), magnetic susceptibility (M/H), and specific heat capacity (Cp).
important_parameters: The coupling is observed near room temperature (around 310 K), and the analysis focuses on the sensitivity of local bonding to magnetic alignment.
main_assumptions: The coupling mechanism is attributed to local bonding rearrangements rather than conventional magnetostriction or macroscopic symmetry breaking.
figures_summary: Figures detail the temperature evolution of lattice parameters and specific bond lengths coinciding with the magnetic anomaly, alongside magnetic susceptibility measurements showing the field-dependent anomaly.
paper_structure: The paper details synthesis and characterization procedures, followed by measurements of magnetic, structural, and thermal properties across a temperature range spanning from cryogenic to above room temperature, culminating in the correlation between structural and magnetic anomalies.
why_interesting: The strong coupling between local atomic structure (bond lengths) and magnetism in a bulk metallic system provides a concrete platform for studying how electronic correlations dictate lattice stability, relevant to understanding emergent quantum phases.
